findings.title: A threshold before the first word
findings.claim: The disjointed letters stand before the first lexical declaration, so the Book is first encountered through an opening that precedes ordinary syntax.
findings.mechanism: The recited letter sequence at 14:1:1:1 meets the immediately following nominative كِتَابٌ at 14:1:2:1; because the first item is not a clause constituent, it acts as a threshold before the Book's declaration.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader feels the transition from voiced opening to named revelation without needing to resolve the letters into a lexical word.
findings.containment: This is a local sequencing effect, not a claim about the letters' definitive interpretation or an external formula.

epistemic.reason: Trusted focus-word evidence and the supplied local wording support this bounded reading.

findings.title: An audible break into the Book

findings.mechanism: The pause marker after الٓر and the next word كِتَابٌ provide a local sound boundary: the recited letters close as a unit before the Book begins.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the Book arrive after a completed opening gesture rather than as part of the same lexical phrase.
findings.containment: The effect is recitational and surface-level; it does not settle a hidden expansion of the letters.

epistemic.reason: Trusted focus-word evidence and the supplied local wording support this bounded reading.

findings.title: The Book as first lexical declaration
findings.claim: After the opening letters, the nominative indefinite كِتَابٌ is presented as the first lexical declaration, foregrounding the Book before its sending is narrated.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader meets the object of revelation as a named reality before being told how it reaches its addressee.

epistemic.reason: Trusted focus-word evidence and the supplied local wording support this bounded reading.

findings.title: A bounded commission under delegated authority
findings.claim: As an attributed reading, the messenger carries out a bounded commission whose authority belongs to the people's Lord and whose force is answerable to a praiseworthy end.

findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive agency as real but bounded: the commission is carried out through authorization and oriented by the final praise.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory, attributed synthesis from a legacy_unbound trace. It does not establish a complete theory of jurisdiction, erase the messenger's grammatical agency, or rank one theological account.
